notes.heading: Entropy as dispersal of matter and energy
points: Entropy, S, measures how widely matter and energy are spread out; more ways to share the energy means higher entropy.
Under the same conditions, entropy order is gas > liquid > solid, since particles gain freedom and energy-sharing options.
Total entropy change = ΔS(system) + ΔS(surroundings).
Standard entropy values S⦵ are in section 13 of the data booklet; units are J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.

notes.heading: Predicting and calculating entropy change
points: To predict the sign of ΔS, check states first, then compare moles of gas on each side.
More gas moles in the products means ΔS is positive; fewer gas moles means ΔS is negative.
Calculation: ΔS⦵ = ΣS⦵(products) − ΣS⦵(reactants), multiplying each value by its balancing coefficient.
Use the right state value: S⦵ of H2O(g) differs greatly from H2O(l). Check the answer against your prediction.

notes.heading: Gibbs energy equation and units
points: ΔG⦵ = ΔH⦵ − TΔS⦵, with T the absolute temperature in kelvin (°C + 273.15).
ΔH and ΔG are in kJ mol⁻¹, but ΔS is in J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. Divide ΔS by 1000 before substituting.
ΔH⦵ comes from bond enthalpies or enthalpies of formation, and ΔS⦵ from standard entropies; thermodynamic data are in the booklet.
ΔG is linked to the energy obtainable from a reaction.

notes.heading: Spontaneity and the sign of ΔG
points: At constant pressure, a change is spontaneous when ΔG < 0.
ΔG includes the system's entropy change and the surroundings' entropy change caused by heat transfer.
ΔH negative with ΔS positive: always spontaneous. ΔH positive with ΔS negative: never spontaneous.
Both ΔH and ΔS positive: spontaneous only at high T. Both negative: spontaneous only at low T.
For ΔH and ΔS both positive, set ΔG = 0 to get T = ΔH/ΔS; above this T the reaction is spontaneous.

notes.heading: ΔG at equilibrium and link to K
points: As a reaction nears equilibrium, ΔG becomes less negative; at equilibrium ΔG = 0, the minimum Gibbs energy.
ΔG = ΔG⦵ + RT lnQ; at equilibrium Q = K, which gives ΔG⦵ = −RT lnK.
Here R = 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, so ΔG⦵ must be in J mol⁻¹. Rearranged: K = e^(−ΔG⦵/RT).
K > 1 means ΔG⦵ < 0 (products favoured); K < 1 means ΔG⦵ > 0 (reactants favoured); K = 1 means ΔG⦵ = 0.
The book says these equations are in section 1 of the data booklet.

definitions.definition: A measure of how dispersed or distributed matter and energy are in a system; the more ways the energy can be distributed, the higher the entropy.
definitions.trap: Describing entropy only as disorder or randomness, which the book calls an oversimplification.

definitions.definition: The entropy change of a reaction under standard conditions, found by subtracting the total standard entropies of reactants from those of products.
definitions.trap: Forgetting to multiply by coefficients or mixing up H2O(l) and H2O(g) values.

definitions.definition: A state function linking enthalpy change, entropy change and absolute temperature, ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, showing the energy obtainable and whether a change is spontaneous.
definitions.trap: Using ΔS in J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ with ΔH in kJ mol⁻¹ without converting.

definitions.definition: At constant pressure, a change with a negative Gibbs energy change, ΔG < 0, which gives an overall increase in total entropy.
definitions.trap: Assuming spontaneous means fast; high activation energy can make it kinetically unfavourable.

definitions.definition: Reactions are spontaneous if they cause an overall increase in total entropy of the system plus surroundings; ΔS total = 0 at equilibrium.
definitions.trap: Looking only at the system's entropy and ignoring the surroundings.

definitions.definition: The ratio of product concentrations to reactant concentrations at any chosen point in a reaction.
definitions.trap: Confusing Q with K, which applies only at equilibrium.

definitions.definition: The ratio of product concentrations to reactant concentrations once a reversible reaction has reached equilibrium, when forward and backward rates are equal.
definitions.trap: Using non-equilibrium concentrations, which gives Q rather than K.
